checks.invariant: One human principal must share starts/concurrency accounting across routes, sessions, nodes, retries, and erasure.
checks.result: SQL quota:22 serializes admission under an actor-fingerprint application lock; rolling starts include released work. Actor-quota:53 derives identity from verified HSA-id and holds it through response completion. Erasure:1272 takes the identical lock and rejects active operations. Cleanup:35 removes only expired entries. Watchdog:7 fail-stops unsettled work before SQL recovery; no attacker-selected quota key or active-budget reset found.

checks.invariant: A single admitted report must not monopolize the shared main event loop or heap beyond effective work limits.
checks.result: Review route:48 builds the model on the server thread after a version-count check. Template:277 calls diffText; text-diff.ts:62 keeps whitespace tokens and :69 allocates the full Cartesian matrix. Two permitted 9,999-character unequal alternating-word fields imply 100 million cells. Synchronous-generation:59-65 checks abort only around this work, so the timer cannot interrupt it. History requires area assignment or Reviewer (:879); the candidate is authenticated.

candidates.title: Review PDF diff expands permitted text into a quadratic main-thread matrix
candidates.description: An area author able to supply a long review revision against a long published or archived baseline, or a Reviewer requesting that report, can trigger disproportionately expensive shared-server work with one admitted PDF request. Two unequal 9,999-character alternating word/space values fit the 10,000-character text limit and tokenize into 9,999 tokens each, causing a 100-million-cell JavaScript number matrix. The source shows synchronous allocation and traversal on the application event loop; no CPU, memory, timeout, or crash observation was performed. Unrelated requests on the same Node process share its heap and event loop. Work persists until completion or process termination; the independent actor watchdog is a late process-wide fail-stop, not per-job interruption.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The accepted field-length limit and report item quota do not constrain the product of diff token counts. Model construction calls the full-matrix LCS synchronously before rendering, while generation cancellation is observed only before and after the callback.

trace.description: Authorizes history access, admits the actor, checks version count, and loads stored text.
Calls buildReviewReport synchronously on the application thread before renderReportModelPdfResponse.
Passes complete description strings into diffText, then repeats for acceptance criteria.

trace.scope: Shared main-thread heap and event-loop work
trace.description: Allocates (oldTokenCount+1)*(newTokenCount+1) cells and visits every cell synchronously, without a token-product cap or abort check.

evidence.description: Business text permits 10,000 characters; alternating single-character words and spaces fit this bound.
Requirement edit description uses businessTextSchema; PUT :232 routes authorized area-author changes into manageRequirement.
History access is available to Reviewer or the assigned area author; this is not anonymous exposure.
Whitespace is retained as tokens, yielding 9,999 tokens for each proposed 9,999-character fixture.
Awaits the entire callback and checks abortion only afterward; a synchronous LCS cannot yield to its timer.
The independent watchdog kills the whole process when its outer deadline expires, preserving accounting but not unrelated process availability.

blockers: Target execution and process isolation are prohibited in this workspace; no bounded growth/cancellation experiment was run.

Actual heap representation, event-loop delay, deployed memory ceiling, and process/supervisor recovery require isolated measurement. A long baseline and review revision must be reachable through the real lifecycle, not merely injected into a unit fixture.

validation_plan.local: In a disposable environment with hard memory/CPU limits, first instrument small unequal alternating-word fixtures (e.g. 128 and 256 tokens) to establish matrix growth and timer starvation without saturation. Use a local synthetic published baseline and authorized review revision to verify the actual route reaches this function under the configured item quota. Do not run the 100-million-cell case; measure allocation counts or replace the allocation with a sentinel in a focused harness.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner confirms Node worker topology, per-process memory limits, supervisor restart behavior, and any existing report isolation or earlier token-product cap. No live load test is needed.

candidates.title: Archive confirmation can remain valid after unarchived child edits
candidates.description: A specification author can commit a needs-reference edit after a PrivacyOfficer exports an eligible obsolete specification. The child update does not change the parent timestamp or the confirmation inputs. Within the same UTC day and 15-minute confirmation lifetime, the PrivacyOfficer can execute disposal with the original token; the newer needs-reference content is deleted although the exported archive contains its previous version. The affected state is the specification owner’s business history. This needs validation of the mandatory archive-preservation guarantee and the real SQL lifecycle; it is not claimed as a role bypass or arbitrary deletion.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The mandatory export confirmation binds candidate identifiers, policy revision, and day-rounded cutoff, but not the exported child content or a revision covering it. The execution transaction rechecks eligibility yet cannot detect a child edit committed between export and execution.

trace.description: Runs the authorized export and returns an export confirmation token with the archive.
Hashes candidate keys, UTC-day cutoff, policy ID and policyUpdatedAt; mintExportToken stores that hash and candidate keys for 15 minutes.
Updates text, description and child updated_at inside a parent-locked transaction, without changing the parent updated_at used for retention selection.
Rebuilds the same candidate set and consumes the unchanged export confirmation; committed child edits are absent from the token comparison.
Deletes specification_needs_references before deleting the specification, including content changed since the archive was produced.

evidence.description: Defines archive export as preserving business history outside the active database; :152 requires anonymized needs references in the export preceding specification disposal.
Eligibility is based on specification.updated_at, lifecycle and active/pending agreements; it does not incorporate needs-reference updated_at.
The cutoff is rounded to midnight, allowing export and later execution on the same day to share a token.
Archive payload includes needs-reference text, description and timestamps, so the later edited content has an identifiable missing archived version.
The child edit is an ordinary authorized manage_specification_needs_reference operation and does not require privacy disposal authority.

blockers: No isolated SQL runtime is permitted, so the export/edit/dispose sequence and persisted archive contents were not exercised.

The owner must confirm that mandatory archive preservation requires the exact deleted child version; if a point-in-time older archive intentionally satisfies the policy, this is a correctness/hardening issue rather than a security finding.

validation_plan.local: Create one synthetic retention-eligible specification with no current/pending agreement and one needs reference. As PrivacyOfficer obtain preview and archive; as its authorized author change the needs-reference text through the real service; on the same UTC day execute disposal using the original tokens. Observe whether execution rejects or deletes the changed text absent from the archive. Use the actual migrations and verify no trigger or workflow touches parent updated_at.
validation_plan.deployment: Information owner confirms the documented archive-before-disposal requirement covers the exact destroyed child content and whether an enforced operational write freeze already prevents this interval.

hardening: lib/pdf/server-response.tsx:20 uses renderToBuffer without checking pdfReportMaxFileBytes, while docs/operations/capacity-management.md:110 describes shared PDF byte limits. Worker memory isolation is explicitly limited to worker-rendered PDFs. No separate resource-impact finding is asserted solely from the missing byte check.

It did not close every taxonomy, requirement-version, requirement-selection, RFI and responsibility-person dependency/cascade path; these require focused policy-specific review rather than inferred coverage.
